content:
This week, Apple continues to steadily expand its Apple Sports app, further enhancing football coverage and providing tennis fans with new ways to follow major tournaments. Here are the details of this update.

Apple Sports adds several football leagues and tennis schedules

When the Apple Sports app first launched, the experience was quite limited in terms of both supported regions and covered sports.

Since then, the app has made progress on both fronts — its availability has expanded to over 170 countries and regions, while continuing to add new sports, leagues, and events.

For example, earlier this year Apple Sports expanded to 90 new countries and introduced multiple features centred around the FIFA World Cup.

This week, Apple Sports received another update, with its football lineup adding the Australian A-League Men, Egyptian Premier League, Israeli Premier League, and South African Premier League.

In addition, the app now allows tennis fans to "follow live draws… including brackets for Grand Slams and 1000-level events," Apple said, enabling users to "see matchups and results for each round at a glance."

Below are the full release notes for Apple Sports 4.4:

Football coverage continues to expand with the addition of the Australian A-League Men, Egyptian Premier League, Israeli Premier League, and South African Premier League. Tennis fans can now use Apple Sports to follow live draws, including brackets for Grand Slams and 1000-level events, making it easy to keep track of matchups and results for each round.

Do you use Apple Sports? Feel free to share with us in the comments.
